# AIS Reconcile — Usage Guide

*Mode: direct · 🔌 offline (no LLM)*

Decrypts an AIS (Annual Information Statement) JSON export entirely in-process -- no manual password entry. The entity is resolved from the export's own filename (the portal names it with a masked PAN prefix, e.g. "XXXDE1234X_2025-26_AIS.json"); that masked prefix is matched against entities.yaml's real PANs, and the decrypt password is derived from the resolved entity's PAN plus DOB (Individual) or DOI (HUF). Always runs the AIS-internal check (l1 detail vs l2 aggregate per element, cross-section TDS-credit total). If a 26AS workbook (this repo's own "26AS" skill output) is also supplied, ties out AIS-reported TDS credit against 26AS's tds_deposited at the aggregate, per-quarter, and per-income-category grain. If a GnuCash book for the SAME financial year is also supplied, ties out AIS income (interest/dividend/salary) and TDS credit against what's actually posted in the books -- this is the primary reconciliation, since the books are the taxpayer's own record of truth. A book for the wrong FY still produces a tie-out sheet but the summary carries an impossible-to-miss WARNING banner. Finally, every flagged delta across all three reconciliations is distilled into a set of ADVISORY suggestions for the AIS portal's own feedback mechanism (e.g. "Information is correct", "Information is not fully correct") -- these are for a human to review before acting on the portal; nothing is ever auto-submitted, and confidence is always capped at low/medium, never high.

## When to use it

Use once you've downloaded your AIS JSON export from the income-tax portal, to check it against itself and (when available) your 26AS and your GnuCash books before relying on it for filing. The books tie-out is the most useful check if your books are kept current -- it's the only one of the three that can actually tell you the AIS is missing or overstating something, not just disagreeing with another government document.

## Inputs

- **Entity (optional) -- fills in the GnuCash book below from the registry** (optional) — accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  - Optional — pick an entity to auto-fill the GnuCash book field from the registered book for that entity.
  - ⚠️ UI convenience only; leave unset to pick the file manually as before. This does not resolve the AIS export's own entity -- that is always inferred from the AIS filename's masked PAN.
- **AIS JSON export (encrypted, as downloaded from the portal)** (required) — accepts: JSON (.json), one export per entity/FY.
  - The AIS JSON export exactly as downloaded from the portal (still encrypted -- decrypted in-process).
  - ⚠️ The filename must keep the portal's own masked-PAN + FY prefix (e.g. "XXXDE1234X_2025-26_..."). If no entity in entities.yaml has a matching PAN, or the matching entity has no DOB/DOI on file, the run fails loud rather than guessing which taxpayer this is.
- **GnuCash book (optional, must be the SAME FY as the AIS -- enables the books tie-out)** (optional) — accepts: GnuCash XML book (.gnucash), optionally gzip-compressed.
  - GnuCash book for the SAME financial year as the AIS export.
  - ⚠️ Must be the matching-FY book. A book with no transactions in that FY window still produces a tie-out sheet, but the run summary carries a loud WARNING -- the numbers on that sheet are almost certainly meaningless for a wrong-year book.
- **26AS workbook (optional, from the 26AS skill -- enables the TDS-credit tie-out)** (optional) — accepts: Excel (.xlsx) with a Part I (TDS) sheet.
  - 26AS workbook produced by this repo's '26AS' skill, for the same entity/year.
  - ⚠️ A workbook for the wrong entity/year will tie out against the wrong TDS figures without a hard error -- double-check before relying on it.

## How to run

1. Pick the AIS JSON export.
2. Optionally supply the matching-FY GnuCash book and/or the entity's 26AS workbook.
3. Click Run -- it decrypts and reconciles offline in a few seconds.
4. Open the Excel workbook: Books Reconciliation and 26AS Tie-out sheets first, then Feedback Suggestions.

## Output

Output is written to the **`Data/outputs/`** folder, named:

```
Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-ais-reconciliation.xlsx
```

Files produced:

- **`YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-ais-reconciliation.xlsx`** — Summary, Books Reconciliation (if a book was supplied), one sheet per AIS section, Flags, 26AS Tie-out (if a workbook was supplied), and Feedback Suggestions (advisory only).

## Tips

The Feedback Suggestions sheet is a starting point for the AIS portal's own feedback form, not something to paste in verbatim -- read the Rationale column and confirm each suggestion against the underlying document before acting on the portal. Confidence is deliberately capped at "low"/"medium": nothing here is ever certain enough to call "high" without a human's own review.

## Troubleshooting

| If… | Then… |
|------|-------|
| "ERROR: no entity ... has a PAN matching the masked prefix". | Add or correct the entity's pan in entities.yaml, or confirm the AIS filename wasn't renamed away from the portal's own masked-PAN_FY_... convention. |
| "ERROR: could not decrypt ...". | The resolved entity's dob/doi in entities.yaml doesn't match what the portal used to encrypt this export -- double-check the date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) on file. |
| WARNING about the GnuCash book having no transactions in the AIS's FY. | You picked the wrong .gnucash book (or the wrong-year one) -- re-run with the book covering the same financial year as the AIS export. |
